title: Repeated-tuple contraction identity
statement: Let X be a scheme, I a linearly ordered type, U : I -> Opens(X) any family, F an abelian-group presheaf, and S a SiteCechComplex for U over the terminal open [def-pc-scheme, def-sc-zariski-site, def-weil-pbc-site-cech-complex]. Let K, kappa and P be the concrete finite-sum operators [def-pc-alternating-cech-sorting-operators]. For every p >= 0, the p-th component of Homotopy.nullHomotopicMap' K equals kappa_p minus P_p. This is precisely dK+Kd=kappa-P, after pulling the repeated-tuple homotopy back by signed stable sorting.

source.place: Tag 01FM, equation 20.23.6.2, pulled back by signed stable sorting

proof.text: Apply the stable-sorting boundary transport to each cochain and tuple. For each sorting permutation, apply the contraction formula to its nondecreasing tuple. Strict monotonicity implies the stable-sort predicate (the equal-entry condition is vacuous). Distribute the finite sum over subtraction. For a stable permutation, split on strict monotonicity; the summand is the stable-sorting summand minus the alternating-projection summand. For a nonstable permutation, strict monotonicity is impossible, so both summands vanish. Equality of morphisms follows from equality on cochains and tuple coordinates.
